what: NSE index freeze quantities revised
detail: Per-order freeze limits from today: Nifty 50 1,800; Bank Nifty 900; FinNifty 1,800; Nifty Midcap Select 2,800; Nifty Next 50 600 (NSE/FAOP/77189 of 30 Oct 2026). They replace the 5 Oct 2026 figures of 3,510 / 1,440 / 3,240 / 5,760 / 1,125; a larger order must still be split.

what: RBI raises the repo rate to 5.50%; stance becomes “calibrated tightening”
detail: The MPC’s 5–7 Oct 2026 meeting raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% (SDF 5.25%, MSF and Bank Rate 5.75%) and changed the stance to calibrated tightening.

what: NSE fixes index freeze quantities (superseded on 2 Nov 2026)
detail: Nifty 3,510; Bank Nifty 1,440; FinNifty 3,240; Midcap Select 5,760; Nifty Next 50 1,125 contracts per order, with the formula method withdrawn for indices (NSE/FAOP/76693). Replaced four weeks later by the 2 Nov 2026 limits.

what: Small-savings rates unchanged for October–December 2026
detail: PPF stays at 7.1%, Senior Citizens’ Savings Scheme 8.2% and NSC 7.7% for the quarter to 31 Dec 2026 (Department of Posts circular reproducing the Ministry of Finance order).

what: CBDT extends the AY 2026-27 audit-case return due date to 21 Nov 2026
detail: The audit report date moved to 21 Oct 2026 and the return for audited cases to 21 Nov 2026. AY 2026-27 is the last year assessed under the 1961 Act.

what: Pre-open order entry runs to 09:10 with a random close
detail: Cash pre-open: order entry 09:00–09:10 with a system-driven random close between 09:08 and 09:10, order matching 09:10–09:12 and a transition buffer to 09:15 (SEBI circular of 16 Jan 2026, implemented by the exchanges).

what: SEBI publishes its FY25–FY26 F&O profitability and trading-behaviour studies
detail: 87.7% of individual equity-derivative traders lost money in FY26, a net ₹91,685 crore; only 0.5% were profitable in all five years FY22–FY26; the FY25 loss was revised to ₹1,11,788 crore on a wider sample. A companion study covers trading behaviour (about 97% of individuals mainly bought options; 59% of index-option turnover was in same-day-expiry contracts).

what: SEBI interim order on expiry-day manipulation in the closing auction
detail: On the 13 Aug 2026 Sensex weekly expiry the indicative index jumped several hundred points within seconds during the Closing Auction Session; two entities holding expiry-day Sensex options were barred from the auction and ₹3.68 crore was impounded.

what: Closing Auction Session starts for stocks with derivatives
detail: Continuous trading in those stocks ends at 15:15; the auction runs 15:15–15:35 with a ±3% band around a reference price (VWAP of the last fifteen minutes); derivatives trade to 15:40; the cash post-close session runs 15:50–16:00; expiring index options settle on the auction-based index close (SEBI circular of 16 Jan 2026).

what: NSE IX stops buy orders in NSE IFSC Receipts (US-stock depositary receipts)
detail: The programme is being wound down under the NSE IX circular of 24 Jul 2026: receipts can be sold until 29 Jan 2027 and converted until 20 Jan 2027, and dealing ends on 1 Feb 2027. The IFSCA Global Access route replaces it for GIFT City access to US stocks.

what: US Section 301 duty of 10% on most Indian goods takes effect
detail: USTR’s Section 301 actions (Federal Register, 28 Jul 2026) impose a 10% tariff on goods of India and sixteen other economies for entries from 24 Jul 2026, with Annex exemptions.

what: SEBI tightens the “education, not advice” test to thirty days
detail: A person engaged solely in investor education must not use market price data of the preceding thirty days (earlier three months) to name a security in a way that indicates its future price or a recommendation (FAQ 8 of circular CIR/2025/11, as updated).

what: Calendar-spread margin benefit withdrawn on expiry day for single-stock derivatives
detail: SEBI’s circular of 5 Feb 2026 extends the expiry-day withdrawal of the calendar-spread margin benefit, in force for index derivatives since February 2025, to stock derivatives expiring that day; spreads between non-expiring months keep the benefit.

what: Income-tax Act 2025 in force; sections renumbered
detail: The new Act and the Income-tax Rules 2026 (notified 20 Mar 2026) apply from tax year 2026-27: speculative transaction s. 66(31), speculation loss s. 113, business loss s. 112, audit s. 63, presumptive scheme s. 58, advance tax ss. 404–408, equity STCG s. 196, LTCG s. 198, returns s. 263.

what: STT on F&O raised by the Finance Act 2026
detail: Finance Act 2026 s. 159 (amending s. 98 of the Finance (No. 2) Act 2004): sale of an option 0.10% → 0.15% of premium; exercised option 0.125% → 0.15% of intrinsic value; sale of futures 0.02% → 0.05%. NSE’s levies page carries the schedule; equity delivery (0.1% each side) and intraday (0.025% on sale) are unchanged.

what: Retail algo framework applies to every broker
detail: Static-IP whitelisting, OAuth with two-factor login and algo tagging become mandatory across brokers; brokers not ready by the glide-path dates were barred from onboarding new API clients from 5 Jan 2026 (SEBI circular of 30 Sep 2025, para 8).

what: Return due date for non-audited business income moves to 31 August
detail: The s. 263(1)(c) table substituted by Act 4 of 2026 applies from tax year 2026-27 (returns filed in 2027): business income without audit 31 August, audited cases 31 October, other assessees 31 July.

what: SEBI Mutual Fund Regulations 2026: index-fund and ETF base expense ratio capped at 0.90%
detail: New expense structure: base ratio caps (index funds and ETFs 0.90%; active equity slabs from 2.10% down to 0.95%), with brokerage and statutory costs shown separately.

what: Sovereign Gold Bond redemption exemption narrowed
detail: Finance Act 2026: the s. 70(1)(x) capital-gains exemption on SGB redemption applies only to individuals who held the bond from the original issue to maturity.

what: TCS on education and medical LRS remittances cut to 2%
detail: Finance Act 2026 amended s. 394 Table Sl. 7(a) of the Income-tax Act 2025 from 5% to 2%; the 20% rate on investment remittances above ₹10 lakh is unchanged.

what: SEBI restates mutual-fund overseas-investment limits
detail: The 2026 Master Circular keeps the industry-wide $7 billion overseas-securities limit and $1 billion overseas-ETF limit, with the per-fund limits and reserved allocation unchanged.

what: NSE transaction charges re-based
detail: Cash segment ₹307 per crore each side (including the ₹0.01 Investor Protection Fund Trust contribution), equity futures ₹183 per crore, equity options ₹3,553 per crore of premium (NSE/FA/73061 of 27 Feb 2026).

what: US Supreme Court strikes down IEEPA tariffs; a 10% Section 122 surcharge follows
detail: Learning Resources v. Trump (decided 20 Feb 2026) held that IEEPA does not authorise tariffs; Proclamation 11012 imposed a temporary 10% import surcharge under s. 122 of the Trade Act for 150 days from 24 Feb 2026.

what: US–India interim trade framework sets an 18% reciprocal tariff
detail: The joint statement of 7 Feb 2026 fixed an 18% reciprocal tariff rate for Indian goods under the interim framework, replacing the IEEPA-based duties of August 2025.

what: Special trading holiday for the Maharashtra municipal elections
detail: NSE and BSE were closed on Thursday 15 Jan 2026, a closure not in the December 2025 holiday circular; it takes the year’s weekday trading holidays to sixteen.

what: NSE index lots cut for the January-2026 expiries
detail: Nifty 50 75 → 65, Bank Nifty 35 → 30, FinNifty 65 → 60, Nifty Midcap Select 140 → 120; Nifty Next 50 stays at 25 (NSE/FAOP/70616 of 3 Oct 2025; weeklies from 6 Jan 2026, monthlies from 27 Jan 2026).

what: LODR: related-party materiality moves to turnover-scaled Schedule XII slabs
detail: The SEBI (LODR) (Fifth Amendment) Regulations 2025 (gazette notification of 18 Nov 2025; this provision in force on the thirtieth day) replace the flat test of ₹1,000 crore or 10% of consolidated turnover, whichever lower, with Schedule XII: 10% of turnover up to ₹20,000 crore; ₹2,000 crore plus 5% of turnover above that up to ₹40,000 crore; ₹3,000 crore plus 2.5% above ₹40,000 crore, capped at ₹5,000 crore. Subsidiaries’ RPTs use the lower of 10% of their own turnover and the listed company’s threshold.

what: F&O pre-open session goes live for current-month futures
detail: Order entry 09:00–09:08, matching 09:08–09:12 and a buffer to 09:15 for current-month index and stock futures; in the last five sessions before expiry it also covers next-month futures (NSE/FAOP/71640).

what: Block deals: minimum ₹25 crore and a ±3% band go live on the exchanges
detail: SEBI’s review of the block-deal framework (circular of 8 Oct 2025, applicable from its sixtieth day, Sunday 7 Dec 2025) replaces the ₹10 crore minimum and ±1% band with ₹25 crore and ±3%, delivery compulsory, in two windows: 08:45–09:00 and 14:05–14:20. NSE and MSEI switched the new parameters on from Monday 8 Dec 2025 (NSE/CMTR/71394), with the band never wider than the stock’s normal-market band that day.

what: Delta-based index-option position limits fully enforced; expiry-day intraday breaches penalised
detail: The end-of-day future-equivalent limits for index options (₹1,500 crore net, ₹10,000 crore gross per PAN) move from the glide path to normal enforcement, and penalties for expiry-day breaches of the intraday limits start.

what: RBI Alert List updated (includes FTMO and FundedNext)
detail: Seven entities added to the list of platforms neither authorised to deal in forex nor to operate forex trading platforms; about 95 are now listed. Absence from the list is not authorisation.

what: Intraday MWPL monitoring for single stocks; non-benchmark index eligibility criteria
detail: Exchanges monitor market-wide position-limit utilisation intraday for single stocks, and a non-benchmark index needs at least fourteen constituents with the top weight at most 20% and the top three at most 45% (SEBI circular of 29 May 2025, implementation table).

what: Intraday index-option position limits: ₹5,000 crore net and ₹10,000 crore gross per entity
detail: SEBI circular of 1 Sep 2025: exchanges take at least four random snapshots a day, including one between 14:45 and 15:30; penalty and surveillance deposit for expiry-day breaches from 6 Dec 2025. This replaces the March 2025 position that intraday breaches were not penalised.

what: MWPL redefined; F&O ban test moves to future-equivalent OI
detail: A stock’s market-wide position limit becomes the lower of 15% of free float and 65 × average daily delivery value (floor 10% of free float), recomputed quarterly; the 95% ban test uses delta-adjusted OI, and trades in a banned stock must reduce end-of-day delta.

what: Retail algo framework goes live for ready brokers
detail: Brokers with systems ready go live; the others follow a glide path — register the API algo product and one strategy by 31 Oct 2025, finish by 30 Nov 2025, mock session by 3 Jan 2026 (SEBI circular of 30 Sep 2025).

what: NPS Multiple Scheme Framework
detail: Non-government subscribers may hold several schemes under one PAN; the highest-risk category allows up to 100% equity (PFRDA circular).

what: Expiry days change: NSE Tuesday, BSE Thursday
detail: Contracts expiring on or after 1 Sep 2025 moved: NSE weekly Nifty 50 options and all NSE monthlies (last Tuesday) to Tuesday, BSE Sensex weeklies and BSE monthlies (last Thursday) to Thursday, under SEBI’s 26 May 2025 circular limiting expiries to those two days (NSE/FAOP/68589; BSE notice 20250617-11).

what: US additional 25% duty on Indian goods (Executive Order 14329) takes effect
detail: An additional 25% ad valorem duty on Indian goods, over the earlier IEEPA reciprocal tariff, citing India’s purchases of Russian oil; the IEEPA-based duties ended after the Supreme Court ruling of 20 Feb 2026.

what: IFSCA revamps the Global Access framework
detail: IFSCA-regulated Global Access Providers in GIFT City may route Indian retail money sent under the LRS to global exchanges; this is the route that later replaced the NSE IFSC Receipts programme.

what: Exchanges publish the retail-algo operational modalities
detail: A 10 orders-per-second threshold for registering self-coded algos; registration turnaround of T+10 working days (T+7 for execution algos); every client API order tagged as an algo order (NSE/INVG/69255; BSE notice 20250723-41).

what: SEBI: FY25 individual F&O losses ₹1,05,603 crore; 91% loss-makers
detail: Comparative study after the October 2024 measures: the number of individual F&O traders fell from 61.4 lakh to 42.7 lakh across FY25 while the loss rate stayed above 90%.

what: Delta-based (future-equivalent) index position limits begin on a glide path
detail: ₹1,500 crore net and ₹10,000 crore gross future-equivalent open interest per PAN for index options, with a T+1 cure period until 5 Dec 2025 and normal enforcement from 6 Dec 2025 (SEBI circular of 29 May 2025).

what: SEBI limits equity-derivative expiries to Tuesday or Thursday per exchange
detail: Every equity derivative of an exchange expires on its chosen weekday; each exchange keeps one weekly benchmark-index option; every other contract has a minimum one-month tenor expiring in the last week of the month; changing the day needs SEBI’s approval.

what: India IIP release moves to the 28th of the month at 16:00 IST
detail: MoSPI shifted the Index of Industrial Production release from the 12th to the 28th (next working day if a holiday), keeping the 16:00 IST time (PIB, 17 Apr 2025).

what: Intraday monitoring of index position limits begins (at least four snapshots)
detail: SEBI measure 5.3 of the 1 Oct 2024 circular: exchanges take at least four random intraday snapshots of index-derivative positions. SEBI’s circular of 28 Mar 2025 said intraday breaches would not be penalised “until further directions”; the separate intraday limits and penalties followed on 1 Oct 2025.

what: TCS threshold on LRS remittances raised to ₹10 lakh
detail: Finance Act 2025 raised the aggregate below which no TCS applies from ₹7 lakh to ₹10 lakh a year; carried into s. 394 Table Sl. 7 of the Income-tax Act 2025.

what: Option premium collected upfront; no calendar-spread benefit on expiry day
detail: SEBI measures 5.1–5.2 (dated 1 Feb 2025) went live on the exchanges on 10 Feb 2025: brokers collect the net option premium from buyers upfront, and the margin offset between expiries is withdrawn on the day the near index contract expires.

what: SEBI issues the retail algo-trading framework
detail: Brokers become principal for API algo orders; exchanges issue algo IDs; algo providers are empanelled with exchanges; white-box and black-box classes; static IP, OAuth and two-factor login for API access.

what: SEBI clarifies the finfluencer rules (FAQs)
detail: Investor education is allowed, but an educator may not use recent market price data to name a security while indicating its future price or a recommendation (then three months; thirty days from 8 May 2026).

what: Research-analyst and investment-adviser regulations overhauled
detail: Amendments introduce part-time registration with a 75-client cap and revised qualification and fee rules; trading calls are research services, not investment advice. Further amendments followed on 10 Feb, 6–7 Aug and 25 Nov 2025.

what: LODR: earnings-call recordings and transcripts within set deadlines
detail: Schedule III para 15(oa): audio of analyst or investor calls within twenty-four hours or before the next trading day, transcripts within five working days.

what: Fewer weeklies, bigger lots, expiry-day margin
detail: One weekly-expiry index per exchange (last weekly expiries: Bank Nifty 13 Nov, Midcap Select 18 Nov, FinNifty 19 Nov 2024); minimum index contract value ₹15 lakh, lots sized to ₹15–20 lakh; an extra 2% ELM on short options on their expiry day (SEBI circular of 1 Oct 2024, paras 5.4–5.6).

what: MoSPI moves CPI and IIP releases to 16:00 IST
detail: Release time changed from 17:30 to 16:00 IST on the 12th of each month (next working day if a holiday), announced 5 Nov 2024.

what: SEBI bars intermediaries from associating with unregistered tipsters
detail: Persons regulated by SEBI, and those acting for them, may not associate with anyone giving unregistered securities advice or making return claims, except through specified digital platforms; existing contracts to end within three months. Pure investor education is carved out.

what: STT on F&O raised (Finance (No. 2) Act 2024)
detail: Sale of an option 0.0625% → 0.1% of premium; exercised option 0.125% of intrinsic value; sale of futures 0.0125% → 0.02%. These rates applied until 31 Mar 2026.

what: SEBI: 91.1% of individual F&O traders lost in FY24; ₹1.81 lakh crore lost over FY22–FY24
detail: Second SEBI profit-and-loss study; more than three in four loss-makers kept trading after two losing years.

what: Equity STCG 20%, LTCG 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh
detail: Finance (No. 2) Act 2024 amended ss. 111A and 112A of the 1961 Act for transfers on or after 23 Jul 2024; the rates are carried into ss. 196 and 198 of the Income-tax Act 2025.

what: LODR: notice for results board meetings cut to two working days
detail: Regulation 29 now requires two working days’ notice (earlier five) of a board meeting that will consider financial results.

what: Optional T+0 settlement starts (beta)
detail: Same-day settlement for a limited set of scrips in a 09:15–13:30 session, alongside the regular T+1 cycle (SEBI circular of 21 Mar 2024); later widened to the top 500 stocks.

what: Last Sovereign Gold Bond tranche closes
detail: SGB 2023-24 Series IV was the final issue; no tranche has opened since and the scheme is in run-off with RBI premature-redemption windows.

what: Debt-fund gains become slab-taxed
detail: Units of funds with more than 65% in debt bought on or after 1 Apr 2023 lose long-term treatment and indexation; the rule now sits in s. 76 of the Income-tax Act 2025.

what: LRS: unused foreign exchange must come back within 180 days
detail: RBI aligned the LRS master direction with FEMA 9(R) Regulation 7: unspent or realised LRS funds must be repatriated within 180 days unless reinvested.
